lectures.title: Time and Space Complexity of AVL Tree

cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to look at time and space complexity of AVL tree.
So here I have only included three methods insert search and delete method.
So these are the methods that are make the AVL tree different from the binary search tree.
Other methods implementation and time and space complexity are same.
So traversal of AVL tree is same as the binary search tree.
That's why I have not included over here.
So here the time complexity for insert method is all again because in this case, after each insertion
we are checking that if the tree is disbalanced, we are making it balanced by using the rotations.
That's why every time a AVL tree will be balanced and in this case, if we insert any node, it's going
to be inserted either in left or right subtree.
That's why the time complexity is all again.
And space complexity is also all again, because here we are using the recursive approach.
That's why we need a login space in the memory for recursive calls.
Now the next method is search method.
So here again the same logic is applicable because whenever we are looking for a node, we are going
to continue to the left or right subtree.
That's why based on the node that we are looking for, we are going to exclude right or left subtree.
That's why in the worst case, the time complexity is going to be all again.
So space complexity is O one over here.
Because in case of search method we are not using recursive approach.
Basically the search method is same as the one that we have implemented in case of binary search tree.
But here in binary search tree there might be cases that the binary search tree looks like the linked
list.
In this case the time complexity is o n.
But in case of AVL tree, as we mentioned, it's going to be a balanced tree.
That's why the time complexity is going to be all again.
So the next method is deleting a node from AVL tree.
So in this case the time complexity is going to be all again because here again we are continuing to
the left or right subtree.
And the space complexity is all again because we are using the recursive approach.
That's why the space complexity is o log n.
So this is the big picture of time and space complexity of AVL tree.
Now in the next lecture let's compare AVL tree with binary search tree in terms of time and space complexity.
